title: p256-ecdlp: parallel Pollard rho on negation classes with a sigma walk

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r) and input Q=[x]P on NIST P-256 the parallel distinguished-point Pollard rho algorithm in proof.md recovers x with probability at least 0.39. It walks on the negation classes {W, −W} of P-256, using 2^32 walks and 2^16 adders, with batched affine additions. The adder coefficients and every trail's coins are drawn from the operating system's randomness, fresh in every run and at every trail start including restarts, independently of the target, and every probability is over the uniform target and these coins. Walks run in trails from fresh coins: each trail ends at its first distinguished point, which it records once, including a distinguished point first reached during a look-ahead. The first key match is resolved by replaying both trails, each replay cut off after 65 times the live steps of its trail (a cut-off replay fails the run), so a degenerate match has probability exactly 1/r (Lemmas R and D). A fruitless cycle is escaped to twice the canonical point of its least-key member, a doubling with no table. Escape points are formally new within their trail, because the order of 2 modulo the P-256 order exceeds twice the trail length bound (D1, verified by accounting.py). A repeated class within a trail is one of three kinds, as in the good event of proof.md: a formal repeat of length at most 64, which is detected and escaped within the per-entry step bound (Lemmas E1 and E2); a formal repeat of length 65 or more, which the good event excludes and whose probability is in DELTA_CUT; or an accidental equality of formally distinct points, bounded by DELTA_LOOP over all trails started (Lemma G, section 2.2), which includes re-entry into an escaped cycle (D2). Every revisit from a fresh class is an entry, at most 128 persistent steps follow each entry (Lemmas E1 and E2, section 2.3). Abandoned trails are bounded by factorial moments over the entries (Lemma T'', section 2.4; DELTA_ABANDON). Fruitless cycles are escaped only after exact checks, and the distinguished-point test comes first on every point. Total computation is at most 2^127.370918 target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing, distinguished-point storage and lookup, all failures and restarts, collision replay, verification and output. Each walk step pays its common-path count, 847 instructions, and a Markov reserve of 40.90 for rare work, that is 887.90 instructions per walk step at C=1000. Rare work is charged at forced-path maxima, measured with a bounding build of each unbatched operation, and the meter aborts when the metered rare work exceeds 64 times its expectation, with probability at most 1/64 (counted in delta). Peak memory is at most 2^76.542441 bytes. Preprocessing is at most 2^47.949581 units and is included in total work. Nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. This is a classical cold attack on one target with no uncharged advice or quantum steps. The success bound of 0.395898 is the model bound 0.411524, less 1/64 for the meter, 2^-20 for the other failure terms, DELTA_CUT (about 6.1·10^-17) and DELTA_ABANDON (about 7.5·10^-8). It relies on the disclosed premises in proof.md: H1, the standard random-mapping model for the collision statistics; and M1, the equivariant random-orientation premise (each class has a uniform key, a canonical representative and a uniform orientation, independent across classes and of x), with the orientation law L-ori (the sign of an arriving point at a fresh class is uniform given the history), which is a measured premise and not a verified law; the entry rates, the abandonment bound and the metered-work reserve use it. The sign transition law, the equal-index forcing and the abab closure law are derived from the definitions. The window premise W (Lemma E1(c)) is a premise: the non-forced transitions of a window are taken to have independent indices and units, and the unit independence is measured at A = 64 (non-forced share 0.5008), not derived. The success bound stays at least 0.39 for an expectation up to about 124 times the premise value. The all-pairs share of a repeated sign is 1/2 + 1/(2A); its excess comes from forced equal-index pairs, which are revisits counted as 2-cycle entries. H3 is the representativeness of the measured instruction counts of the common path, with rare work charged at forced-path maxima; it is a measurement assumption. These are supported by toy-curve runs of the identical procedure and by production-curve measurements, not proved. This is a carefully accounted generic attack, not a claim of a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Run the complete procedure of proof.md section 1.3 on random prime-order toy curves y^2=x^3-3x+b (the P-256 shape), at budget tau = tau_e4/10^4: each slot runs trails from fresh coins without tracking coefficients, with the same class key, canonical rule, adder images and index, both cycle rules and escapes; a trail ends at its first distinguished point, recorded once with its coins, or is abandoned at the cap; each slot takes L steps and finishes its trail. The first key match is resolved by replaying both trails from their coins, each replay cut off after 65 times the live steps of its trail (a cut-off replay fails) (with a different anchor schedule, checking Lemma R); a degenerate match fails. The filters compare keys masked to filter_bits, as the kernels keep only 64 key bits, and the distinguished-point test precedes every escape and every look-ahead step; with check_all_replays every recorded trail is also replayed and any replay that misses its recorded point is counted. The filters compare keys masked to filter_bits, as the kernels keep only 64 key bits, and the distinguished-point test precedes every escape and every look-ahead step; with check_all_replays every recorded trail is also replayed and any replay that misses its recorded point is counted. Reports the success rate against 1-exp(-tau), degenerate matches and replay mismatches. No oracle collision table. Toy scale only: it tests the procedure and its collision statistics, not production cost.
Recompute the claimed time_log2, preprocessing, memory and success lower bound from the stated parameters with exact integer arithmetic, and check the order of 2 modulo r used by D1 (proof.md 2.1).
